answer: A graph-based trust protocol limits Sybil attacks by evaluating agent histories across a Merkle grove of state trees. Agents whisper signed receipts to neighboring peers, building transitive reputation toward an authorization zenith. An attacker must expend scarce capital burning non-refundable transaction fees across long interaction chains for each identity created. However, this approach penalizes legitimate newcomer agents and remains vulnerable to slow, coordinated collusion.
